9dd0cb68e26133b1.description: HanmiGlobal Saudi is seeking an experienced Mechanical Engineer with a strong irrigation background to join our client-side programme and construction management (PMCM) team on a major government land-development and infrastructure programme in Riyadh. A Lead Developer designs and builds the programme’s infrastructure, including roads, water, sewer, storm drainage, power and street lighting, irrigation, landscape and telecom. Our team reviews, supervises and accepts that work on the client’s behalf. The Mechanical Engineer will oversee the irrigation and pumping systems serving the programme’s parks, streetscapes and public realm on an assigned package. The role covers design and submittal review, site supervision, and testing and commissioning through to handover. It involves close coordination with the landscape, utilities, drainage and electrical disciplines, the developer’s contractors and the relevant utility authorities. Key Responsibilities Review irrigation and mechanical design submissions, hydraulic and water-demand calculations, drawings, shop drawings and material submittals for irrigation networks, pump stations, pipelines, valves, filtration and control systems, checking compliance with the approved specifications and client standards. Supervise and inspect irrigation and mechanical works on site against the approved drawings, specifications and quality procedures. Witness and verify testing and commissioning, including hydrostatic pressure tests for pipelines, pump operational and performance tests, network flushing, and commissioning of controllers and central control systems. Ensure that failed tests are corrected and re-tested. Process and track Work and Material Inspection Requests (WIRs/MIRs), and raise and follow up Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) for the discipline. Review water-supply, TSE, storage and pumping provisions, and give feedback on maintainability, sustainability and life-cycle performance. Support value engineering and constructability reviews. Coordinate interfaces with the landscape, water, drainage and electrical disciplines, and with utility providers on connections, tie-ins and authority witnessing. Review close-out deliverables, including as-built drawings, O&M manuals and plans, warranty certificates, spare-parts lists and commissioning certificates. Witness the contractor’s training of operations staff on the irrigation systems. Guide the package Mechanical and Irrigation Inspectors, and contribute to progress reports and site meetings. Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related discipline (e.g., Agricultural or Irrigation Engineering with a strong mechanical and pumping background). More than 15 years of experience on infrastructure, land-development or large-scale landscape projects, with substantial hands-on experience in irrigation and pumping systems. Client-side experience as a PMC/PMCM, owner’s engineer or supervision consultant. Strong knowledge of irrigation networks (drip, bubbler, sprinkler), pump stations, hydraulics, pipelines (HDPE, uPVC, DI), valves, filtration and fertigation, and controllers and central control systems. Proven experience witnessing testing and commissioning of pipelines and pumps. Registration with the Saudi Council of Engineers (SCE). Proficient in CAD and hydraulic analysis tools, and in inspection and quality documentation. Excellent reporting, communication and coordination skills, and the ability to work with contractors, developers and utility authorities. Professional written and spoken English and/or Arabic. Both are an advantage. Preferred: KSA/GCC experience, TSE irrigation systems, familiarity with Saudi codes and utility-authority standards, and the ability to join within 30 days of an offer.

9de5a3d22e129dff.description: About Kerten Hospitality Kerten Hospitality (KH) operates as an end-to-end lifestyle hospitality provider, focusing on creating bespoke destinations, lodging, experiences, and communities. The company aims to optimize operations and drive profitability for investors while maintaining a strong commitment to sustainability. 9dd9c08795f8e888.description: We are hiring a Venture Capital Associate to grow our network of investors who invest directly in private companies, and to manage those relationships over time. Pairs is a global network of family offices, institutional investors, VCs and angels. We screen deal flow very tightly, and the opportunities that clear our diligence go out to the network. We invest alongside them too. THE ROLE This role sits on the investor side of Pairs. You bring in investors who back companies directly, understand what each of them looks for, and introduce them to opportunities that fit. You also open new investor relationships every month, using the same approach that built your existing ones. You know which investors in your network have made a direct investment in the past year, what they invest in, and at what stage and check size. When a founder needs qualified investor meetings at short notice, you know whom to approach first. We are not raising a fund. Our investors invest directly in companies, so a network made up mainly of fund LPs or institutional mandates is not the right fit for this role, however strong it is. Our platform handles the pipeline, research and follow-up. Your time goes to investor conversations, and to judging which investors are ready to commit capital. You will work directly with the two co-founders and our investor team. The organisation is flat, so you will see first-hand how we screen opportunities, what we decline and why. Your current title matters less than the quality of your relationships. We are looking for someone who has built those relationships personally and can explain exactly how. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Your investor relationships. The investors you bring and those you add here, kept current and qualified. They remain yours. Network growth. New relationships every month with family offices, high-net-worth individuals and angel investors who are new to Pairs. Investor matching. A clear understanding of what each investor looks for, so the opportunities you share are relevant. Ongoing engagement. Staying useful to investors between opportunities, so they continue to work with us. YOU ARE A FIT IF YOU Have built your investor relationships personally, and can explain how each one began: direct outreach, referrals you cultivated, or events and networks you engaged with deliberately. Have taken at least one investor from a first conversation to a direct investment in a private round, and can walk us through the process. Understand what your investors invest in: stage, check size, sector, and the reasons they decline. Treat discretion as second nature. Please do not include any investor names in your application. Use AI tools daily, with clear judgement about where they improve your work and where they would compromise its quality. WHAT WE OFFER A fully remote, asynchronous role Direct access to the co-founders and our investor team Close collaboration with our internal team Live mandates from your first week, and access to the opportunities that clear our diligence Insight into our internal processes, including how we screen deal flow A base salary plus commission

9d39fd5a4da3db55.description: JOB PURPOSE The Senior Manager of Digital Health & Technology leads the definition, prioritisation and delivery readiness of QHC’s healthcare digital, data and technology requirements. The role translates clinical, operational and corporate priorities into clear technology requirements, delivery roadmaps, information flows and reporting needs, while coordinating with QIC / QTech on solution design, architecture alignment, implementation planning and service readiness. In a healthcare startup, technology is a critical enabler of clinical operations, reporting, integration and patient experience. The role supports prioritization of the systems required across Sports Medicine, Citywide Healthcare and IHN, and tracks technology dependencies, delivery risks and readiness requirements. Specifically, within Sport Medicine / Performance , technology is core infrastructure rather than a support afterthought: electronic health records, clinical and athlete-monitoring platforms, analytics and cybersecurity must be specified, procured, deployed and integrated to enable safe clinical delivery and evidence-based performance health. The role works closely with clinical, operations, finance and enabling teams to translate business and clinical needs into healthcare technology and data requirements, coordinating with function owners and QTech to ensure solutions are aligned with healthcare requirements and that data is usable for decision-making. The role also supports technology quality assurance, readiness and compliance with relevant healthcare-specific technology and data requirements. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES 1. Digital Health Strategy & Technology Requirements • Implement approved QHC Digital Blueprint and define QHC's health technology requirements and digital roadmap across clinical, operational and enabling domains, aligned with the organization's startup priorities and target operating model. • Translate clinical and business needs into technology specifications, architecture principles and a prioritized delivery plan. • Advise leadership on build-versus-leverage decisions across the QIC / QTech and partner ecosystem. • Coordinate with QTech and relevant function owners on interoperability and integration requirements across clinical, operational and administrative systems. 3. Data Management, Analytics & Business Intelligence • Define QHC’s healthcare data requirements, information flows, data ownership and reporting needs across functions. • Define and coordinate analytics and reporting requirements that support data-driven clinical, operational and leadership decision-making. • Track data availability, quality, ownership and reporting gaps, coordinating with function owners to ensure healthcare data is usable for decision-making. • Support reporting and data needs across the organization as capability matures. 4. QTech / QIC SLA & Vendor Service Delivery • Define, establish and manage service-level agreements with QIC / QTech and technology partners, ensuring strong, accountable service delivery to QHC. • Monitor vendor and partner performance against SLAs and drive remediation where service falls short. • Act as the primary QHC coordination point with QTech and relevant technology stakeholders on healthcare-specific technology requirements and delivery priorities. 5. Cybersecurity, Data Privacy & Governance • In coordination with QIC, embed cybersecurity, data privacy and information-governance controls across all platforms and data flows from the outset. • In coordination with QIC, ensure compliance with Saudi data-protection and healthcare information regulations and applicable international standards. • In coordination with QIC, establish access controls, audit trails and incident-response readiness for health and personal data. 6. Deployment, Integration & Readiness • Oversee deployment and integration readiness for all technology, ensuring systems are tested, secure and operational ahead of go-live milestones. • Coordinate healthcare-specific testing and readiness activities with QTech and relevant clinical and operational teams. • Track technology readiness against the enterprise activation roadmap. 7. Innovation & Digital Enablement • Identify and introduce digital health innovations — telehealth, remote athlete monitoring, wearables and AI-assisted tools — aligned with partner best practice. • Pilot and scale digital solutions that enhance clinical quality, athlete outcomes and operational efficiency. EXPERIENCE & ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Health Informatics, Engineering, or a related field is required. A Master's degree and recognized certifications (e.g. health informatics, cybersecurity, TOGAF, ITIL, or vendor platform certifications 8+ years of progressive experience in digital health, healthcare IT, health informatics or technology delivery, including experience defining healthcare technology requirements, supporting EHR and healthcare platform delivery, and coordinating technology readiness in new or transforming organizations. Demonstrated experience managing technology vendors and SLAs, data management and analytics, and cybersecurity / data-privacy controls within a healthcare environment. Experience within accredited healthcare institutions (JCI, CBAHI) is an advantage. Working knowledge of Saudi data-protection and healthcare information regulatory frameworks, and of interoperability and integration across clinical and administrative systems.
